primary_gameplan: Cycle Street Wraith/Generous Ent/Curator of Mysteries to load the graveyard and hold Subtlety, not Force of Negation, for Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler; cascade off Violent Outburst or Shardless Agent once the graveyard is loaded and no Vexing Bauble is on their battlefield.
secondary_gameplan: If the cascade window closes (a resolved Vexing Bauble, or a Drannith Magistrate off Green Sun's Zenith), fall back to Damping Matrix and Dismember on the mana engine, Force of Vigor on Leyline of Abundance, and hard-cast Wistfulness with {G}{G} to exile the enchantment while Endurance and Subtlety hold the board.
opponent_gameplan: Badgermole Cub and Leyline of Abundance each read 'Whenever you tap a creature for mana, add an additional {G}', so with one down a Devoted Druid taps for two green and with both down for three. Devoted Druid's own 'Put a -1/-1 counter on this creature: Untap this creature' recurs that, free and unbounded once the 1-of Vizier of Remedies reduces the counter to zero, and once per turn regardless off Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler's '+1: Untap up to one target creature'. Green Sun's Zenith and Nature's Rhythm convert the pile of green into Craterhoof Behemoth, or into Walking Ballista where the list runs one. Delighted Halfling's second mana ability makes any legendary spell it pays for uncounterable, which is how Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler resolves through Force of Negation.
pitfalls: Treating this row as a second archetype. Across 10 recent top-8 lists per label, `devoted combo` and this wiki's `creatures toolbox` share an identical seven-card four-of core -- 4 Badgermole Cub, 4 Delighted Halfling, 4 Devoted Druid, 4 Green Sun's Zenith, 4 Nature's Rhythm, 4 Leyline of Abundance, 4 Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler -- present in 20 of 20 lists, plus 2 Birds of Paradise in 20 of 20. The rest of the shell is near-universal rather than universal, and the exact counts matter because they are the evidence: Vizier of Remedies is 1-of in 18 of 20 and a 2-of in decks 879293 and 878822; Fiend Artisan is a 2-of in deck 878794; Duskwatch Recruiter is absent from deck 879067; and Underground Mortuary is absent from decks 882367 and 879293, the latter running Lair of the Hydra instead. They are ONE deck under two unmerged archetype ids (c4fc27b7-4e36-4b08-a070-4d5824a6d1a6 versus c22029ff-3de2-424e-85bc-c270daf9558a), and the labels are temporally disjoint -- zero `creatures toolbox` decks dated on or after 2026-08-13, zero `devoted combo` decks dated on or before 2026-08-10, overlapping only on 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-12 (decks 879293 and 879301). This is a relabel, so `creatures toolbox` is the retired id. The shares are NOT double-counted: `shares` partitions 100pp over deck counts at 0.074683pp per deck, so 43 + 44 = 87 decks = 6.4974pp is this deck's true single share and a slot serving both rows is credited once per half. What the split does cost is ranking - 6.4974pp is the field's #3 archetype, behind instant reanimator and broodscale bloodchief, and each half reads as an #8/#9 - and currency, because only the 44 recent lists reflect the live board.

Expecting Subtlety to ANSWER Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler. Two separate errors sit here. First, Force of Negation is dead on a Tyvar the opponent paid for with Delighted Halfling's SECOND ability ('{T}: Add one mana of any color. Spend this mana only to cast a legendary spell, and that spell can't be countered') -- but only then. Halfling's first ability is '{T}: Add {C}' and confers no uncounterability at all, so an untapped Halfling is a warning, not a rule. Second, Subtlety is not the answer: its OWNER chooses, and the text is 'Its owner puts it on their choice of the top or bottom of their library'. Against a resolved-on-the-stack Tyvar they take top and recast it next turn, so Subtlety buys one turn here and nothing more. Treat it as a tempo card in this matchup, not as removal.

Reading Damping Matrix as a total lock here. Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler's '+1: Untap up to one target creature' is a LOYALTY ability of a planeswalker, not an activated ability of an artifact or a creature, so Damping Matrix does not touch it -- and Tyvar is a 4-of in 10 of 10 pulled lists. Matrix shuts off the free repeating Devoted Druid untap, Walking Ballista, Agatha's Soul Cauldron, Fiend Artisan and Duskwatch Recruiter; it leaves them one untap per turn.

Tapping out for Damping Matrix into open {B}{G}. Abrupt Decay ('This spell can't be countered. Destroy target nonland permanent with mana value 3 or less') is in 8 of 10 pulled sideboards and Damping Matrix is exactly mana value 3, so it is the single worst artifact in the 15 to walk into their untapped duals. Force of Vigor is in 7 of 10 and Boseiju, Who Endures is maindeck in 10 of 10.

Boarding Tormod's Crypt. It is mana value 0 and a legal cascade hit under Violent Outburst/Shardless Agent's mana value 3, their engine is on the battlefield rather than in the graveyard, and Collector Ouphe ('Activated abilities of artifacts can't be activated') is in 9 of 10 pulled sideboards -- absent only from deck 881870 -- which blanks the Crypt's only ability outright.

Assuming Endurance's graveyard clause is dead here, as this wiki's `creatures toolbox` sidecar says. Nature's Rhythm has 'Harmonize {X}{G}{G}{G}{G} (You may cast this card from your graveyard for its harmonize cost...)' and is a 4-of in 10 of 10 lists, and Dewdrop Cure ('Return up to two target creature cards each with mana value 2 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield') is in 4 of 10 sideboards. The strip mode has real targets in this matchup.

Repeating this wiki's `creatures toolbox` claim that Damping Matrix is symmetric_counter against our own cycling. It is not, and the contradiction is resolved under stance_rationale: CR 109.2 scopes 'artifacts and creatures' to permanents on the battlefield, and a Street Wraith being cycled is a creature CARD in a hand.

stance_rationale: Dismember kills every relevant body in the engine (Devoted Druid 0/2, Badgermole Cub 2/2, Vizier of Remedies 2/1, Delighted Halfling 1/2), Force of Vigor destroys two of Leyline of Abundance / Agatha's Soul Cauldron / Vexing Bauble off-turn for no mana, and Damping Matrix turns off the free Devoted Druid untap loop, Walking Ballista, Agatha's Soul Cauldron, Fiend Artisan and Duskwatch Recruiter. All three are mana value 3-4, clear of the Violent Outburst / Shardless Agent cascade floor of 3. Damping Matrix is a `counter`, NOT a `symmetric_counter`, and this wiki's two sidecars disagree about that -- `broodscale-bloodchief.json` is right and `creatures-toolbox.json` is wrong. The rules chain: Damping Matrix reads 'Activated abilities of artifacts and creatures can't be activated unless they're mana abilities'; those descriptions name card types, name no zone, and use none of the words 'card', 'spell' or 'source', so CR 109.2 makes them mean permanents of that type on the battlefield, and CR 403.3 ('Permanents exist only on the battlefield') closes it. A Street Wraith being cycled is a creature CARD in a hand, never a 'creature', so its cycling is untouched -- as are Curator of Mysteries, Generous Ent, Oliphaunt, Colossal Skyturtle's channel and Waker of Waves's discard ability, which are all activated from hand. CR 702.29b, which `creatures-toolbox.json` cites the other way, says only that the cycling ability continues to EXIST in other zones so that effects keying off the presence of an ability can see it; it does not put a card in hand inside the set of objects CR 109.2 built. The real cost of Damping Matrix in this matchup is not symmetry, it is their removal: Abrupt Decay (8 of 10 sideboards, uncounterable, and Matrix is exactly mana value 3), Force of Vigor (7 of 10), Guerrilla Gorilla (6 of 10), Chomping Changeling (5 of 10) and maindeck Boseiju, Who Endures (10 of 10). It is still a counter -- each of those is a card they must draw and spend -- but it is a more contested one here than against the `creatures toolbox` label of the same deck.
